scope: Matched held-out tournament of rank-16 H3 topology-LoRA epoch-0 checkpoints and a deployment-scale ablation
summary: Both rank-16 adapters remove the baseline head-to-torso and stable-proportion failure categories on the 124-frame demo, but neither repairs the raised-arm shoulder origin and both regress frozen worst-frame identity and motion, so no checkpoint is promoted.
evidence: The unchanged backbone fails left-shoulder attachment in 100 frames, stable proportions in 100 frames, and the head-to-torso chain in 82 frames; only 24/124 frames pass the full topology conjunction.

r1 epoch-0 and r2 epoch-0 retain only the 100 left-shoulder failures: the 82 head-to-torso failures and 100 stable-proportion failures are absent in digest-bound full-frame review, although the total fully passing frames remain 24/124.
r1 epoch-0 worst-frame DINOv2 identity is 0.7890441418 versus 0.8833816648 for baseline, and matched motion adherence is 0.9083083743; it is rejected.

r2 epoch-0 worst-frame DINOv2 identity is 0.8658662438 and matched motion adherence is 0.9685012815; it is the least-regressing structural candidate but still fails the 0.01 identity-gain and motion non-regression contract.

The r2 scale-0.5 ablation recovers worst-frame identity to 0.8800596893 but motion remains 0.9546766267 and all three baseline topology failure categories return, so scale reduction does not preserve the structural gain.
Scene preservation and temporal consistency pass their non-regression gates for all three measured candidates.
lessons: The topology-positive curriculum can selectively stabilize a robot torso and head chain, demonstrating a measurable native backbone adaptation effect rather than a post-process.
The remaining shoulder-origin error is not solved by more generic topology repetition or lower LoRA strength; the next dataset revision must supervise unique shoulder attachment more directly.
LoRA scale is a real capability tradeoff: weakening the adapter restores appearance identity but also removes the structural improvement.
limitations: All candidates use third-party NF4 MiniMax-H3 weights and one held-out 124-frame real-scene action.
The structural improvement is partial: fully passing topology frames remain 24/124, and no candidate passes the release contract.
The full-frame labels are 2-D semantic review bound to video digests, not 3-D kinematic evidence or real-robot execution.
Epoch-1 checkpoints were not used to claim an improvement because epoch-0 already exposed identity and motion regression.
next_actions: Revise the training set with camera-matched raised-arm examples, explicit shoulder-origin crops, and hard negatives for arms emerging from the neck or head.
Add at least three held-out identities, scenes, and actions before any release claim, and retain the current demo as a frozen regression case.
Evaluate the official BF16 H3 base separately before publishing an adapter intended for broad use.
